name: Raft
desc: Logs or reeds lashed into a floating platform; likely used in the first sea crossings to Sahul.

name: Sledge
desc: A runner-borne platform dragged over snow, ice or ground; among the earliest land vehicles.

name: Travois
desc: Two poles dragged in a V by a dog or horse to carry loads without wheels.

name: Pack animal
desc: Donkeys, camels, llamas and horses loaded with goods, the backbone of overland trade.

name: Yoke
desc: A wooden beam joining draft animals so they can pull a plough or cart together.

name: Corduroy road
desc: Logs laid across wet ground to make a passable track, as in Britain's Sweet Track.

name: Wagon
desc: A four-wheeled load vehicle, carrying more than a two-wheeled cart.

name: Domestication of the horse
desc: Taming and breeding horses, the fastest land transport until the railway.

name: Bit
desc: A mouthpiece with reins that lets a rider or driver steer and stop a horse.

name: Horseback riding
desc: Riding horses for travel, herding and war, which shrank distances on the steppe.

name: Spoked wheel
desc: A light wheel of hub, spokes and rim that made fast vehicles possible.

name: Chariot
desc: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used for war, racing and status.

name: Wheelbarrow
desc: A single-wheeled hand cart that lets one person move heavy loads.

name: Saddle
desc: A padded seat on a horse's back that spreads the rider's weight and improves control.

name: Stirrup
desc: Foot loops hung from the saddle that steady the rider; spread from China across Eurasia.

name: Hipposandal
desc: A Roman strapped-on iron sandal protecting horses' hooves on hard roads.

name: Horseshoe
desc: A nailed iron shoe protecting hooves, letting horses work on hard and wet ground.

name: Horse collar
desc: A padded collar letting horses pull with full strength without choking.

name: Odometer
desc: A geared device counting wheel turns to measure distance travelled.

name: South-pointing chariot
desc: An ancient Chinese two-wheeled cart whose geared mechanism kept a pointer aimed in a fixed direction as it turned.

name: Diolkos
desc: A paved trackway with grooves for hauling ships across the Isthmus of Corinth.

name: Roman roads
desc: Engineered, layered and drained roads that bound the Roman Empire together.

name: Coach
desc: A covered carriage with a suspended body, first built at Kocs in Hungary.

name: Horse-drawn omnibus
desc: A large coach running a fixed route for paying passengers, the first public transit.

name: Leaf spring
desc: Stacked steel strips forming a spring that cushions vehicles from road shocks.

name: Differential
desc: A gear train letting wheels on one axle turn at different speeds when cornering.

name: Reed boat
desc: Bundled reed hulls used on the Nile, in Mesopotamia and on Lake Titicaca.

name: Plank boat
desc: Planked hulls stitched or pegged together, allowing larger ships than dugouts.

name: Oar
desc: A pole with a blade levered against the hull to row boats.

name: Steering oar
desc: A large oar at the stern used to steer ships before the rudder.

name: Harbor
desc: A sheltered anchorage with quays, as at Wadi al-Jarf in Egypt.

name: Outrigger boat
desc: A canoe stabilized by floats on booms, carrying Austronesians across oceans.

name: Catamaran
desc: A twin-hulled vessel with great stability, developed by Austronesian seafarers.

name: Crab claw sail
desc: A triangular Austronesian sail giving strong lift for ocean voyaging.

name: Polynesian navigation
desc: Wayfinding by stars, swells and birds that settled the remote Pacific.

name: Galley
desc: A long ship propelled mainly by oars, dominant in the Mediterranean for millennia.

name: Trireme
desc: A fast galley with three banks of oars and a bronze ram.

name: Dry dock
desc: A basin that can be drained to build or repair a ship's hull.

name: Canal
desc: An artificial waterway for navigation linking rivers and seas.

name: Flash lock
desc: A removable barrier that releases a surge of water to carry boats past a weir.

name: Grand Canal
desc: The longest canal in the world, linking northern and southern China.

name: Pound lock
desc: A chamber with gates at both ends that raises or lowers boats between levels.

name: Rudder
desc: A hinged blade on the sternpost that steers large ships effectively.

name: Junk
desc: A Chinese sailing ship with battened sails and a stern rudder.

name: Watertight compartment
desc: Bulkheads dividing a hull so one breach does not sink the ship.

name: Lateen sail
desc: A triangular fore-and-aft sail allowing ships to sail closer to the wind.

name: Dhow
desc: A lateen-rigged trading ship of the Indian Ocean and Red Sea.

name: Clinker construction
desc: Overlapping planks riveted together, the hull method of northern Europe.

name: Longship
desc: A long, shallow Viking ship under sail and oar, reaching from Vinland to Constantinople.

name: Cog
desc: A flat-bottomed, single-masted merchant ship of the Hanseatic League.

name: Carvel construction
desc: Frame-first hulls with flush planks, allowing larger and stronger ships.

name: Portolan chart
desc: Sea charts drawn from compass bearings and distances between ports.

name: Carrack
desc: A large three- or four-masted ocean ship that carried the voyages of exploration.

name: Caravel
desc: A small, nimble Portuguese ship able to sail upwind along African coasts.

name: Full-rigged ship
desc: A ship with three or more square-rigged masts, the standard oceangoing vessel.

name: Galleon
desc: A large multi-decked sailing ship used for trade and war, as on the Manila route.

name: Submarine
desc: A vessel that can operate underwater; first built by Cornelis Drebbel.

name: Canal du Midi
desc: A summit-level canal linking the Atlantic and Mediterranean across France.

name: Clipper
desc: A sharp-hulled, heavily canvassed sailing ship built for speed.

name: Paddle steamer
desc: A vessel driven by steam-powered paddle wheels.

name: Electric boat
desc: A battery-powered boat, first demonstrated by Moritz von Jacobi on the Neva.

name: Screw propeller
desc: A rotating helical blade that drives ships more efficiently than paddles.

name: SS Great Britain
desc: Brunel's iron-hulled, screw-driven ship, the forerunner of modern liners.

name: Ocean liner
desc: A ship running scheduled passenger service across oceans.

name: Roll-on/roll-off ship
desc: Vessels that vehicles drive or roll onto, starting with railway train ferries.

name: Bulk carrier
desc: A ship carrying unpackaged cargo such as coal, ore or grain in holds.

name: Ironclad
desc: A steam-powered warship protected by iron armor plates.

name: Icebreaker
desc: A ship with a strengthened hull that breaks ice to keep sea lanes open.

name: Suez Canal
desc: A sea-level canal joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea, shortening Europe to Asia routes.

name: Refrigerated ship
desc: A ship with refrigerated holds for meat and fruit, opening global food trade.

name: Oil tanker
desc: A ship that carries oil in bulk in its hull tanks.

name: Motorboat
desc: A small boat driven by an internal combustion engine.

name: Turbinia
desc: The first steam turbine ship, far faster than any vessel of its day.

name: Motor ship
desc: A ship powered by a diesel engine rather than steam.

name: Hydrofoil
desc: A boat lifted on underwater wings, cutting drag at speed.

name: Panama Canal
desc: A lock canal across Panama joining the Atlantic and Pacific.

name: Bathyscaphe
desc: A free-diving deep-sea craft with a float and pressure sphere; Trieste reached the Challenger Deep in 1960.

name: Nuclear marine propulsion
desc: A shipboard reactor that lets vessels run for years without refueling.

name: NS Savannah
desc: The first nuclear-powered merchant ship.

name: Intermodal container
desc: A standard steel box moved between ship, rail and truck without unpacking.

name: Container ship
desc: A ship built to carry intermodal containers, the engine of modern globalization.

name: Container crane
desc: A dockside gantry crane that loads and unloads containers rapidly.

name: LNG carrier
desc: A ship with insulated tanks carrying liquefied natural gas.

name: Hovercraft
desc: A vehicle riding on a cushion of air over land and water.

name: Supertanker
desc: Crude oil tankers of 200,000 tonnes and more, enabled by huge welded hulls.

name: Yara Birkeland
desc: A battery-electric container ship designed for autonomous operation.

name: Wagonway
desc: Wooden rails guiding horse-drawn wagons at mines, the ancestor of railways.

name: Tram
desc: Street rail vehicles for passengers, first horse-drawn at Swansea.

name: Rack railway
desc: A railway with a toothed rail engaging a cog to climb steep grades.

name: Liverpool and Manchester Railway
desc: The first intercity railway relying entirely on steam locomotives.

name: Bogie
desc: A pivoting wheeled truck that lets long rail vehicles take curves.

name: Wire rope
desc: Twisted metal wires forming a strong cable for mines, cable cars and bridges.

name: Railway signal
desc: Fixed signals telling train drivers whether the line ahead is clear.

name: Railway time
desc: Standardized clock time across a network, the origin of time zones.

name: Interlocking
desc: Mechanisms preventing conflicting signal and switch settings.

name: Funicular
desc: A cable railway with counterbalanced cars on a steep slope.

name: Rapid transit
desc: High-capacity urban railways on separated tracks, starting with London's Metropolitan Railway.

name: Elevated railway
desc: Urban railways carried above streets on viaducts.

name: Railway air brake
desc: Westinghouse's compressed-air brake acting on every car of a train.

name: Cable car
desc: Streetcars gripping a moving underground cable, as in San Francisco.

name: Refrigerator car
desc: A chilled rail car that let meat and produce travel long distances.

name: Electric locomotive
desc: A locomotive powered by electricity, first demonstrated by Siemens in Berlin.

name: Electric tram
desc: The world's first commercially successful electric tramway, in Berlin.

name: Overhead line
desc: Wires above the track that feed power to trains, trams and trolleybuses.

name: Regenerative braking
desc: Braking by using a motor as a generator to recover energy.

name: Third rail
desc: A conductor rail alongside or between the running rails that supplies power to trains; first demonstrated by Siemens in 1879, used on London's deep tube from 1890.

name: Multiple unit
desc: Self-propelled cars controlled together from one cab, standard for commuter trains.

name: Monorail
desc: A railway running on a single rail or beam, as on the Wuppertal Schwebebahn.

name: Aerial tramway
desc: Cabins suspended from cables carrying passengers up mountains.

name: Diesel locomotive
desc: A locomotive powered by a diesel engine, which replaced steam worldwide.

name: Centralized traffic control
desc: Remote control of signals and switches over a whole line from one office.

name: High-speed rail
desc: Dedicated lines and trains running above 200 km/h.

name: Shinkansen
desc: Japan's high-speed rail network, opened between Tokyo and Osaka.

name: Automatic train operation
desc: Computer control of train driving, from London's Victoria line to driverless metros.

name: Light rail
desc: Modern tram-like urban rail on partly segregated tracks.

name: Maglev
desc: Trains levitated and propelled by magnetic fields, with no wheel contact.

name: SCMaglev
desc: Japan's superconducting maglev, which set the rail speed record of 603 km/h.

name: Hydrogen train
desc: The first passenger train powered by hydrogen fuel cells in regular service.

name: Dandy horse
desc: Karl Drais's two-wheeled running machine, the first bicycle.

name: Velocipede
desc: Pedal-driven bicycle with cranks on the front wheel.

name: Wire wheel
desc: A light wheel with tensioned wire spokes.

name: Penny-farthing
desc: A high-wheel bicycle with a large direct-drive front wheel.

name: Roller chain
desc: A bushed chain transmitting power between sprockets, key to the bicycle.

name: Safety bicycle
desc: A chain-driven bicycle with equal wheels, the form still used today.

name: Pneumatic tire
desc: An air-filled rubber tire that cushioned bicycles and later cars.

name: Motorcycle
desc: A two-wheeled motor vehicle, first built by Daimler and Maybach.

name: Bicycle-sharing system
desc: Public bicycles available for short-term use, later automated with docks and apps.

name: Electric bicycle
desc: A bicycle with a battery-powered motor assisting the rider.

name: Fardier à vapeur
desc: Cugnot's steam tractor, the first self-propelled land vehicle.

name: Electric car
desc: A car powered by an electric motor and batteries, first by Gustave Trouvé.

name: Carburetor
desc: A device mixing fuel and air for gasoline engines.

name: Manual transmission
desc: A driver-shifted gearbox matching engine speed to road speed.

name: Bus
desc: A motor vehicle carrying many passengers on fixed routes.

name: Truck
desc: A motor vehicle built to carry freight.

name: Taxicab
desc: A car for hire with a driver, charging by meter.

name: Semi-trailer truck
desc: A tractor unit hauling a detachable semi-trailer, the main freight carrier on roads.

name: Hybrid electric vehicle
desc: A vehicle combining an engine and electric drive, from Lohner-Porsche to the Prius.

name: Continuous track
desc: An endless band of plates spreading a vehicle's weight over soft ground.

name: Drum brake
desc: Shoes pressing outward against a rotating drum to slow a wheel.

name: Disc brake
desc: Pads clamping a rotating disc, giving strong, fade-resistant braking.

name: Spark plug
desc: A plug firing a high-voltage spark to ignite fuel in an engine cylinder.

name: Filling station
desc: A roadside facility selling fuel to motorists.

name: Ford Model T
desc: The cheap, durable car that made motoring a mass phenomenon.

name: Electric starter
desc: An electric motor that cranks the engine, ending hand cranking.

name: Hydraulic brake
desc: Brakes actuated by fluid pressure, applying even force at every wheel.

name: Turbocharger
desc: An exhaust-driven turbine compressor that boosts engine power.

name: Automatic transmission
desc: A gearbox that shifts by itself, first mass-produced as GM's Hydra-Matic.

name: Seat belt
desc: A harness holding occupants in place in a crash; the three-point belt came in 1959.

name: Crumple zone
desc: Car body sections designed to deform and absorb crash energy.

name: Fuel injection
desc: Metered injection of fuel into engine cylinders or intakes.

name: Fuel cell vehicle
desc: A vehicle powered by a hydrogen fuel cell driving an electric motor.

name: Engine control unit
desc: An electronic computer managing fuel, ignition and emissions.

name: Airbag
desc: A cushion that inflates in a crash to protect occupants.

name: Catalytic converter
desc: An exhaust device that turns pollutants into less harmful gases.

name: Anti-lock braking system
desc: Electronic control that stops wheels locking under hard braking.

name: Automotive navigation system
desc: In-car route guidance using satellite positioning and digital maps.

name: Electronic stability control
desc: Braking individual wheels automatically to prevent skids.

name: Adaptive cruise control
desc: Cruise control that keeps a safe gap to the vehicle ahead.

name: Toyota Prius
desc: The first mass-produced hybrid car.

name: Battery electric vehicle
desc: A vehicle powered solely by an on-board battery pack driving electric motors, with no combustion engine or fuel cell.

name: Self-driving car
desc: A car that senses its surroundings and drives itself, first demonstrated in the 1980s.

name: Ride-hailing
desc: App-based services matching passengers with drivers in real time.

name: Robotaxi
desc: Driverless taxis carrying paying passengers without a safety driver.

name: Trolleybus
desc: An electric bus drawing power from twin overhead wires.

name: Bus rapid transit
desc: Buses on dedicated lanes with stations, as pioneered in Curitiba.

name: Radial tire
desc: A tire with cords running across the tread, longer-lasting and safer.

name: Macadam
desc: Roads of compacted layers of broken stone, devised by John McAdam.

name: Asphalt concrete
desc: Aggregate bound with bitumen, the most common road surface.

name: Tarmac
desc: Macadam bound with tar, patented by Edgar Purnell Hooley.

name: Traffic light
desc: Signals controlling traffic at intersections; electric versions from 1912.

name: Road surface marking
desc: Painted lines and symbols guiding traffic on the road surface.

name: Controlled-access highway
desc: A divided highway without at-grade crossings, from Italy's autostrade.

name: Parking meter
desc: A coin-operated timer charging for kerbside parking.

name: Interstate Highway System
desc: The US national network of controlled-access highways.

name: Ski
desc: Long wooden runners strapped to the feet for gliding over snow.

name: Snowshoe
desc: A wide frame worn on the foot to spread weight and walk on deep snow.

name: Dog sled
desc: A sled hauled by teams of dogs, enabling travel and freight across Arctic regions.

name: Kayak
desc: A narrow skin-covered Arctic boat paddled with a double-bladed paddle.

name: Stagecoach
desc: Coaches running scheduled long-distance stages with fresh horses at each stop.

name: Ackermann steering geometry
desc: A linkage letting inner and outer wheels turn at different angles on a curve.

name: Rickshaw
desc: A light two-wheeled cart pulled by a runner, widespread in Asian cities.

name: Bireme
desc: A galley with two banks of oars, used by Phoenicians and Greeks.

name: Knarr
desc: A broad Norse cargo ship that carried settlers to Iceland and Greenland.

name: Chip log
desc: A knotted line and sandglass for measuring a ship's speed in knots.

name: Fluyt
desc: A cheap, capacious Dutch cargo ship that underpinned Dutch trade dominance.

name: Gaff rig
desc: A four-sided fore-and-aft sail set from a spar, efficient with small crews.

name: Schooner
desc: A fast fore-and-aft rigged ship with two or more masts.

name: Copper sheathing
desc: Copper plating on hulls to stop shipworm and fouling, making ships faster.

name: Bridgewater Canal
desc: A coal canal that cut transport costs and launched Britain's canal age.

name: Windjammer
desc: A large iron- or steel-hulled sailing cargo ship of the late sail era.

name: Ship model basin
desc: A towing tank where scale models predict hull resistance, pioneered by William Froude.

name: Boat lift
desc: A machine that raises boats between canal levels in water-filled caissons.

name: Outboard motor
desc: A detachable engine and propeller unit clamped to a boat's stern.

name: Bulbous bow
desc: A bulb below a ship's waterline that reduces wave-making drag.

name: Rotor ship
desc: A ship using spinning Flettner rotors and the Magnus effect for thrust.

name: Pump-jet
desc: A ducted water jet propulsor for shallow-draft and fast craft.

name: Autonomous underwater vehicle
desc: An untethered robotic submarine that runs preprogrammed missions.

name: Remotely operated underwater vehicle
desc: A tethered robot submarine controlled from the surface.

name: Automatic identification system
desc: Ship transponders broadcasting position and identity to prevent collisions.

name: Stephenson's Rocket
desc: The multitube-boiler locomotive that won the Rainhill Trials.

name: Sleeping car
desc: A railway carriage with berths for overnight travel.

name: Traction engine
desc: A self-propelled steam engine for hauling loads on roads and farms.

name: Road roller
desc: A heavy roller that compacts road surfaces, first steam-powered.

name: First transcontinental railroad
desc: The line linking the US east and west coasts.

name: Janney coupler
desc: An automatic knuckle coupler that made joining rail cars safer.

name: City and South London Railway
desc: The first deep-level electric underground railway.

name: Chairlift
desc: Open chairs on a moving cable loop, carrying skiers uphill.

name: Gas turbine locomotive
desc: A locomotive powered by a gas turbine driving generators.

name: Tilting train
desc: Trains that lean into curves so they can run faster on existing track.

name: Personal rapid transit
desc: Small automated pods on guideways, first at Morgantown, West Virginia.

name: TGV
desc: France's high-speed train, holder of the conventional rail speed record.

name: Shanghai maglev
desc: The first commercial high-speed maglev line.

name: Derailleur gears
desc: Multiple sprockets and a chain-shifting mechanism for bicycle gearing.

name: Motor scooter
desc: A step-through motorcycle with small wheels, popularized by the Vespa.

name: Scooter-sharing system
desc: App-rented dockless electric scooters in cities.

name: Speedometer
desc: An instrument showing a vehicle's speed.

name: Headlamp
desc: Lamps lighting the road ahead of a vehicle.

name: Shock absorber
desc: A damper that controls spring motion for a smooth, stable ride.

name: Windshield wiper
desc: A blade sweeping rain from a vehicle's windscreen.

name: Four-wheel drive
desc: Driving all four wheels for traction off-road and in snow.

name: Forklift
desc: A powered truck with forks for lifting and moving loads.

name: Pallet
desc: A flat platform letting goods be handled as one unit by forklifts.

name: Car radio
desc: A radio receiver built into a car.

name: Snowmobile
desc: A tracked motor vehicle on skis for travel over snow.

name: Power steering
desc: Hydraulic or electric assistance that reduces steering effort.

name: Cruise control
desc: A system holding a car at a set speed without the driver's foot.

name: Continuously variable transmission
desc: A transmission with a continuous range of gear ratios, first built by Milton Reeves in 1879 and later used in cars.

name: Electronic toll collection
desc: Radio tags that let vehicles pay tolls without stopping.

name: Lane departure warning system
desc: Cameras that warn a driver drifting out of lane.

name: DARPA Grand Challenge
desc: Robot vehicle races that catalysed modern autonomous driving.

name: Plug-in hybrid
desc: A hybrid whose battery can be charged from the grid for electric-only driving.

name: Roundabout
desc: A circular intersection where traffic flows around a central island.

name: Cloverleaf interchange
desc: A two-level junction with loop ramps eliminating left turns across traffic.

name: Cat's eye
desc: Retroreflecting road studs that mark lanes at night.
